forces.title: High financing costs hinder new property investment and cost absorption
forces.description: Higher interest rates and increased construction costs are making businesses and non-residential investors more cautious about investing in new commercial properties across Europe. Furthermore, these elevated financing costs make it significantly more difficult for governments, non-residential investors, and homebuyers to absorb rising input costs, thereby capping overall momentum in the construction sector and limiting profitability for developers and contractors.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Geopolitical risks and uncertainty dampen commercial real estate investment
forces.description: Heightened geopolitical uncertainty, particularly stemming from conflicts like the Iran war and Middle East tensions, is making commercial real estate investors more cautious. This uncertainty caps momentum in new developments and transactions, as it increases reluctance to commit to long-term projects and exacerbates concerns over energy prices and supply chain disruptions, impacting the financial viability and attractiveness of new-builds.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising construction and renovation costs challenge project viability and asset upgrades
forces.description: Increased energy prices are elevating production costs for energy-intensive building materials such as concrete, cement, and bricks, contributing to higher overall construction and renovation expenses. These rising costs make new-build projects less financially viable and increase the expense of upgrading existing commercial assets to meet modern standards, particularly for sustainability improvements. This pressure is making it harder for builders and developers to pass on costs to buyers, impacting profitability.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Execution bottlenecks delay office and logistics development in Netherlands
forces.description: Execution constraints, specifically grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions, are becoming more prominent in the Netherlands. These issues lead to delays in project delivery and increase the number of permitted projects awaiting construction starts. Such bottlenecks are expected to constrain residential, office, and logistics development more frequently in the coming years, directly impacting the supply and timing of new commercial real estate assets.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Moderate Dutch economic growth and stable interest rates support demand
forces.description: The Dutch economy is experiencing modest growth, supported by wage growth and government spending, demonstrating increased resilience to new energy price shocks. Coupled with expectations of relatively stable capital market interest rates, these factors are helping to stabilize financing costs for investors and underpin investor demand in the commercial real estate market. This provides a moderately positive economic backdrop amidst various headwinds.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Foreign investors retreat from Dutch real estate due to tax and regulation
forces.description: Foreign investors have largely exited the Dutch real estate market in recent years, shifting demand primarily to domestic investors. This retreat is largely attributed to tax changes, including a stepwise increase in transfer tax, and the introduction of residential rent regulation. This represents a structural shift in the investor base, potentially limiting capital inflows and altering market dynamics for commercial properties in the Netherlands.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: ESG and climate policies reduce appeal of outdated office buildings
forces.description: Institutional investors are increasingly focusing on societal impact, driven by stricter climate policy expectations and their own ESG policies. This has led to a significant decline in interest for outdated office buildings that lack a financially viable sustainability pathway. Such properties are becoming less attractive for acquisition and disposal decisions, indicating a structural imperative for modern, energy-efficient office spaces.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: E-commerce shift leads to declining retail real estate stock
forces.description: The structural shift towards online shopping, potentially accelerated by the rise of agentic commerce, continues to impact the retail real estate sector in the Netherlands. This trend is leading to an overall decline in the retail real estate stock and concentrating investor demand predominantly in prime retail locations where vacancy risks are considered relatively limited, signifying a long-term contraction for non-prime retail assets.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Defence spending fuels demand for European industrial and logistics real estate
forces.description: The surge in European defence spending, driven by NATO commitments to raise defence budgets and the EU's push for domestic production, is creating a new and credible demand driver for industrial and logistics property. This includes demand for specialized manufacturing space, increased stockpiling facilities with long-term leases, and R&D parks, providing a significant and long-term tailwind for the sector, potentially adding 8-20% to demand.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Tariffs and e-commerce normalization create logistics real estate headwinds
forces.description: The European logistics property sector faces headwinds from tariffs, which have made occupiers more cautious in their leasing decisions. Additionally, the normalization of the e-commerce boom, which previously fueled significant demand, means that the sector is looking for new demand drivers. These factors collectively temper the momentum for logistics real estate, making the search for new growth catalysts like defence spending critical.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Energy transition drives demand for well-located, charging-ready logistics assets
forces.description: The energy transition is pushing logistics players towards electrification, making access to sufficient (or scalable) charging infrastructure a critical factor. This trend favors larger, well-located logistics assets that can meet these evolving energy demands. Such properties are expected to perform better and gain increasing importance in investment and location decisions due to their operational efficiency benefits and their ability to support the sustainability goals of logistics operators.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: AI and private equity enable capture of 'dark value' in CRE
forces.description: The commercial real estate sector is witnessing a shift from traditional 'buy-and-hold' models, driven by the reduced cost of AI and machine learning tools for identifying arbitrage opportunities. The influx of private equity investors, willing to disrupt conventional practices, further accelerates this trend. These factors enable players to systematically capture 'dark value' through short- and medium-term optimization strategies, enhancing returns by 3 to 5 percentage points annually for agile firms.
forces.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

forces.title: CRE market frictions create opportunities for agile investors
forces.description: The commercial real estate sector is characterized by structural frictions, including high transaction costs, complex regulations, asset heterogeneity, and information asymmetry, which historically lead to low market liquidity and slow transactions. However, these very friction points are now being recognized as sources of 'dark value' for investors capable of leveraging insights and agility to identify arbitrage opportunities and reposition capital or assets faster than the broader market.
forces.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

forces.title: Conservative culture and rigid governance hinder CRE market agility
forces.description: The commercial real estate industry's slow pace and conservative mindset are major obstacles to capturing short- and medium-term 'dark value' opportunities. Centralized and hierarchical governance structures among investors slow down decision-making and stifle initiative. To effectively leverage market signals and opportunities, the sector requires a fundamental cultural shift towards managing risk and a transformation of governance to empower front-line decision-making, which is currently lacking.
forces.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

forces.title: Strong in-store retail reinvigoration boosts Irish retail real estate investment
forces.description: Investor interest in Irish retail parks and shopping centers is robust, driven by a post-pandemic reinvigoration of in-store retail activity. High occupancy levels (over 95% nationwide) and the continuous opening of new international brands like Lego and Arket underscore the sector's positive momentum. This strong operational performance directly translates into sustained funding activity for property purchases and extensive store revamps, indicating continued confidence in retail real estate assets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Commercial construction strengthens with sustained new order inflows in Ireland
forces.description: Commercial construction activity in Ireland is experiencing the strongest growth within the broader construction sector, marking a third successive month of expansion. This uplift is primarily supported by sustained new order inflows, indicating robust underlying demand for commercial properties. The broad-based recovery in this segment contrasts with the weaker performance of housing, positioning commercial construction as a key driver for the Irish real estate market's current positive momentum.

forces.title: Cost inflation and staff shortages pose risks for Irish commercial construction
forces.description: The Irish construction sector, including commercial construction, faces persistent key risks from cost inflation, staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times. These factors necessitate that firms build flexibility into their contracts, stress-test project margins, and closely manage their exposure to supply-chain partners who may be reliant on short-term credit. While overall sentiment has improved, maintaining financial discipline and risk management remains crucial for a sustainable recovery in commercial building projects.

forces.title: Dutch residential transfer tax reduction temporarily boosts commercial real estate
forces.description: A reduction in the transfer tax for residential real estate in the Netherlands (from 10.4% to 8%) as of 2026 appears to have provided a temporary boost to commercial real estate investment volumes in the first quarter of 2026. This was because investors postponed residential real estate transactions to the new year to benefit from the lower tax rate, indirectly influencing the overall real estate market figures, a temporary effect that has since faded.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Dutch commercial real estate recovery is fragile despite strong Q1 investment growth
viewpoints.description: The Dutch commercial real estate market experienced a strong start to 2026, with Q1 investment volumes up more than 60% year-on-year, partly boosted by a residential transfer tax reduction. However, this recovery is expected to slow in H2 2026 due to heightened geopolitical uncertainty, rising construction and renovation costs, and execution bottlenecks. These factors are making new developments less financially viable and increasing costs for existing assets, indicating a less robust underlying momentum.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Significant untapped value in commercial real estate through short-term optimization strategies
viewpoints.description: Commercial real estate investors are currently overlooking opportunities to boost returns by over one-third, missing an estimated $200 billion in global value annually. This 'dark value' can be captured by shifting from a traditional 'buy-and-hold' model to more flexible, short- and medium-term optimization strategies, supported by AI-enabled tools. The sector's inherent friction points like high transaction costs and complex regulations, while challenging, also create arbitrage opportunities for agile investors.
viewpoints.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

viewpoints.title: Europe's defence spending to drive long-term logistics real estate demand
viewpoints.description: Increased defence spending across Europe, driven by NATO targets and EU domestic production goals, is emerging as a credible and long-term demand anchor for the industrial and logistics property sector. This push for local production, expanded stockpiling, and R&D investment is expected to add 8-20% to demand for logistics space in the coming years. While a significant tailwind, the impact will be fragmented and often result in build-to-own facilities, with 20-30% as leasehold opportunities.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

viewpoints.title: Irish retail park and shopping centre investment remains robust post-pandemic
viewpoints.description: Investor interest in Irish retail parks and shopping centres is strong, evidenced by notable transactions across key regions over the past year. This is attributed to a post-pandemic reinvigoration of in-store retail, with numerous international brands opening new stores and occupancy levels returning to over 95% nationwide. Bank of Ireland reports robust funding activity for store purchases and revamp proposals, indicating continued confidence in the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Outdated Dutch office buildings face declining institutional investor interest due to ESG factors
viewpoints.description: Institutional investors are increasingly prioritizing societal impact, stringent climate policies, and their own ESG guidelines. This shift is causing a decline in interest for outdated office buildings in the Netherlands that lack a financially viable pathway to sustainability improvements. Such properties are becoming less attractive for acquisition and disposal decisions, reflecting a structural change in investment criteria for the office sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Dutch retail real estate stock declining amid ongoing shift to online shopping
viewpoints.description: The Dutch retail real estate market is experiencing an overall decline in stock, a direct consequence of the structural shift towards online shopping, potentially accelerated by agentic commerce. Investor demand is increasingly concentrated in prime retail locations, where vacancy risks are perceived as relatively limited. This trend indicates a challenging environment for non-prime retail properties and a shrinking footprint for the sector as a whole.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Dutch logistics real estate remains attractive despite investor caution and rising vacancies
viewpoints.description: The Dutch logistics real estate market, while experiencing increased investor caution and rising vacancy rates outside traditional hotspots, remains attractive due to its strategic location and role as a transit hub. The energy transition is pushing for electrification, making larger, well-located assets with sufficient charging infrastructure particularly important for efficient operations and investment decisions, signaling continued demand for high-quality properties.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Commercial construction leading growth in strengthening Irish construction sector
viewpoints.description: Irish construction activity continues to strengthen for a third consecutive month, driven by sustained new order inflows. Commercial construction is experiencing the strongest growth within the sector, with civil engineering also at its highest level since 2022. In contrast, housing remains the weakest-performing segment due to taxation and rent-cap policies, positioning commercial projects as a primary driver of the broader construction recovery in Ireland.

demand_drivers.description: A reduction in residential real estate transfer tax from 10.4% to 8% in 2026 encouraged investors to postpone transactions to the new year, which temporarily boosted commercial real estate investment volumes in Q1 2026.

market_sizing.methodology: The Dutch commercial real estate market investment volume in Q1 2026 was more than 60% higher than a year earlier. This surge was partially attributed to investors postponing residential real estate transactions to the new year due to a reduction in transfer tax from 10.4% to 8% for residential property as of 2026, indirectly boosting commercial real estate figures.
market_sizing.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

new_opportunities.description: Capturing 'dark value' through strategies similar to commodity traders, leveraging AI-enabled tools, and exploiting market frictions like high transaction costs and information asymmetry.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated annual value worldwide in commercial real estate that investors are missing out on by not adopting short- and medium-term optimization strategies. Calculated through internal analysis.
market_sizing.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

demand_drivers.driver: Increased defence spending by NATO members
demand_drivers.description: Commitment to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP and 1.5% for infrastructure by 2035 drives demand for industrial and logistics infrastructure.

demand_drivers.driver: Shift to local production and supply chain resilience
demand_drivers.description: EU targets for domestic defence procurement and NATO's focus on stockpiling and supply chain resilience require more space for manufacturing, assembly, storage, and distribution.

market_sizing.methodology: Savills' optimistic estimate for additional industrial and logistics demand across Europe and the UK if NATO members converge to a 3.5% defence spending target by 2033. This is compared to an existing defence-related industrial and logistics space of 35-40 million square metres, representing 9-10% of total inventory (JLL, Q4 2025: 400 million sqm).
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

demand_drivers.description: European defence push, reindustrialization, and supply chain resilience initiatives are expected to generate additional demand for industrial and logistics real estate.

market_sizing.methodology: Green Street's conservative estimate for additional defence-related industrial and logistics demand through 2035.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

demand_drivers.description: Government intention to exempt defence spending from budget control measures and a €500bn fund for infrastructure spending support logistics demand.

market_sizing.methodology: GARBE Industrial's estimate for demand for the institutional market and investors in Germany from 2025 to 2030, related to defence spending. This translates to a potential uplift of 8-15% for Europe when extrapolated using Germany's annual take-up of 5.3-5.4m sqm.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

demand_drivers.description: NATO members pledging to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP and 1.5% for infrastructure by 2035, driving demand for logistics space.
Most defence-related demand is for bespoke, specialised, secure, and strategic facilities, with 20-30% of this new space expected to be leasehold for institutional investors.

market_sizing.methodology: The potential share of annual logistics take-up from the defence sector across Europe could rise to between 8-20%, with a base case of 14%. This translates to an annual institutional opportunity of 0.5m to 1.25m sqm of additional leased space per year.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…
